discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can produce a time-reversal-invariant topological phase, the quantum spin Hall insulator, classified by a Z2 invariant. This idea was later extended to three-dimensional topological insulators. In 2007 Molenkamp's group observed quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, the first experimental realization of this new state of matter. Together these works created a field: topology became an organizing principle for band insulators, and research grew on topological superconductors, Weyl semimetals and magnetic topological phases. A direct outcome was the quantum anomalous Hall effect, achieved in magnetically doped topological insulator films and in MnBi2Te4. This is now pursued as a route to resistance metrology and topological quantum devices. It is a rare case of a theoretical concept and a precise transport experiment together revealing an entirely new state of matter, and of a discovery that has changed condensed matter physics.
